questions.prompt: Which country has the capital city Warsaw?

hints.nudge: Every country has one capital city. Find the city in the question on a map, then see which country it sits in.
hints.whereToLook: Look on the Atlas: find the city, then see which country it sits in.

questions.proof: The capital city of Poland is Warsaw.

questions.prompt: Which of these countries shares a border with Poland?

hints.nudge: Two countries are neighbours when you can walk from one into the other. Picture Poland on the globe and look at what it touches.
hints.whereToLook: Look in the “Geography” part of the Poland article.

questions.proof: Szczecin Lagoon is on the western border with Germany.

questions.prompt: Which of these countries covers the most ground?

hints.nudge: Area is how much ground a country covers, not how many people live there. A small crowded country can still be small.
hints.whereToLook: Compare the four on the Atlas. Area means how much ground a country covers.

questions.proof: By area: Poland about 312,683 square kilometres; Syria about 185,180 square kilometres; Azerbaijan about 86,600 square kilometres; Moldova about 33,844 square kilometres.

questions.prompt: What is the capital city of Poland?

hints.nudge: A capital city is where a country’s government meets. The other three are capital cities too, of other countries.
hints.whereToLook: Look in the opening paragraphs of the Poland article.

questions.proof: Most Polish people live in large cities, including the capital, Warsaw, Łódź, Cracow, the second capital of Poland (first was Gniezno), Szczecin, Gdańsk, Wrocław and Poznań.
